National Heritage Board · 6 sites · Shared block library

One block library for six museum sites

Every block variant detected on the six sites (351 per-site variants, 3,734 instances) was reviewed visually and mapped onto a shared Edge Delivery Services block and variant. Similar components become one block with a variant option instead of a per-site copy; rich text with no component behaviour becomes default content.

Default content

174 per-site variants (1,179 instances) are body copy: headings, paragraphs, lists, inline images, buttons, legal text and layout tables used only for formatting. In EDS these are authored as normal document content — no block code. By site: ACM 40 · IHC 41 · MHC 24 · NMS 54 · PM 10 · SYSNMH 5.

Method

  • Input: the block catalogs of the six site analyses (every live page rendered; block instances cropped and grouped into structural variants per site).
  • Each per-site variant's representative screenshot was reviewed on labelled contact sheets and assigned to a shared block/variant by appearance and purpose — not by markup, which differs in detail even where components are the same.
  • Instance counts come from the analyses; a page can contain several instances of one variant.
  • Only the main content area was catalogued. Components placed in the site header or footer (e.g. breadcrumbs on ACM/NMS, newsletter sign-ups in footers) are not counted, so an empty cell means "not detected in page content", not necessarily "absent from the site". Header/footer are migrated separately as EDS nav and footer fragments.
  • The mapping is in nhb-shared-block-library.mapping.json (site, per-site variant key, shared block, shared variant) for use when writing import parsers.
